# Radu Bebe — enemies, weapons, and hints

- Original source: [Radu Bebe — enemies, weapons, and hints](https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/pc/562021-robin-hood-the-legend-of-sherwood/faqs/23711)
- Author / publication: Radu Bebe (Radu_Bebe) / GameFAQs
- Language / date: English; version 1.0, updated 2003-06-02
- Access: Live page blocked (HTTP 403); text read from the Wayback Machine capture
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09, from the 2019-06-02 capture
- Archived copy: [Wayback Machine, 2019-06-02](https://web.archive.org/web/20190602032627/https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/pc/562021-robin-hood-the-legend-of-sherwood/faqs/23711)
- Format: header notes, original summary, then detailed factual notes (no permission notice in the guide, so not transcribed)

A complementary mechanics FAQ rather than a complete campaign route. It organizes observations into changes from earlier tactics games, enemy categories, weapons, and practical hints.

The author describes assigning unused recruits to production or training in Sherwood, and taking generic recruits on easier ambushes while heroes improve their skills. Archery training reportedly requires an arrow in the trainee's inventory without consuming it. Recruitment is associated with the proportion of enemies spared.

Enemy notes distinguish officers, ranged soldiers, heavily armored opponents, mounted enemies, and civilians who raise alarms. Weapon notes compare lethal and nonlethal options, including the difference between Robin's punch and Little John's stronger knockout.

**Limitations:** the author explicitly invents some enemy names, estimates mission totals, and marks several observations as uncertain. Numeric damage and training claims need verification against the relevant difficulty and game version before becoming implementation requirements.

## Detailed notes

Guide title as printed: "ROBIN HOOD -- THE LEGEND OF SHERWOOD -- GAME GUIDE -- V 1.0", by Radu Bebe, updated 06/02/03. Six sections: Intro, What's new?, Enemies, Weapons, Hints, Credits. The credits thank the "DLH webpage" for hosting, which suggests the FAQ first appeared on dlh.net. The guide carries no permission or reproduction notice, so it is not reproduced verbatim here; the full text is in the archived copy linked above.

### Intro and "What's new?"

- Calls the game a real-time tactics title that is "pretty much the same as Desperados" but more complex than Desperados and Commandos; controls are familiar from both.
- **Sherwood base between missions:** cottages/tables produce items; an old soldier trains melee; targets train archery. Archery training only works if the trainee has at least one arrow in the bag; the arrow is not consumed.
- **Two character classes.** Merry Men (main heroes, recruited by rescuing them; listed in order of appearance as Stuteley, Will Scarlet, Maid Marian, Little John, Friar Tuck) have three actions plus a special ability. Workers come in three body types (tall, hunchbacked, normal height; the author calls them big, small and normal workers), have two actions plus a special ability, are best kept at home producing, and are good for the easy early money ambushes. New workers appear after each normal mission in proportion to the spared-lives percentage.
- **Four mission types:** normal story missions (rescues, warnings), ambushes for the ransom (three forest maps), "blazon" missions on the same forest maps where every enemy must be removed to stop Prince John's attacks, and two castle missions with allied squads where all enemies must be eliminated. The author guesses "about 40 missions".

### Enemies (names invented by the author)

| Class | Type | Author's observations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weak | Foot soldier | Most common; spear; little health; "almost harmless" |
| Weak | "Sworder" | Sword and shield; extra armour |
| Weak | "Blader" | Long axe; low damage |
| Weak | Archer | Lowest health; arrows do 10 damage; retreats and shoots again when approached |
| Weak | Crossbowman | Very slow first reload (can be knocked out meanwhile); after the first shot reloads faster; bolts do 20 damage |
| Strong | "Governor" (officer) | More health than a Merry Man; orders subordinates to attack first; leads large troops; troops report to him |
| Strong | Knight | Armoured, arrows bounce off; huge sword; can knock a hero out in one hit; lets others attack first; subordinate to the officer |
| Strong | Rider (cavalry) | About 20 in the game; charges and knocks out everyone near the target; mace does up to 50 damage; kill him once knocked out; riders (and possibly knights) do not carry off tied or unconscious soldiers |
| Strong | General | Army leaders, usually die last; only Robin duels them; 3–4 in the game |

Soldier colours: blue (first missions, weakest), orange (most missions, normal), red (harder, many missions), black (last missions, very strong), green (allies). Well-dressed civilians (a woman in a long red-pink skirt, a man in blue) raise the alarm and bring soldiers.

### Weapons, items and abilities (author's usefulness rating out of 10)

Melee: fist (Robin, Little John; knocks out from behind; Robin cannot KO knights or officers, only Little John can) 5. Staff (Little John; Robin in ambushes only; one-shot KO on weak soldiers, at most four hits on strong) 8. Sword (Robin outside ambushes, Marian, normal workers; kills, rarely knocks out; also cuts drawbridge ropes) 7. Axe (Stuteley; like a shorter sword) 6. Mace (Will Scarlet; kills quickly, overhead hits can KO strong enemies in one blow, can finish unconscious enemies) 8. Sceptre (Friar Tuck; small, fast, good damage) 6. Club (big workers; low damage, KOs every type like the staff) 6. Fork (small workers; long reach, sometimes KOs, can kill unconscious) 6. Shield (Will, normal worker; blocks arrows but the bearer is hit about 80% of the time) unrated.

Ranged: bow (Robin, Marian, normal worker; one-shots weak soldiers, two for officers, cannot target important NPCs or generals, useless against knights and riders) 9. Slingshot (Will; KOs weak soldiers in one shot, officers in one or two, never knights or riders; long range) 7.

Items: net (Stuteley; short throw, holds a group until freed) 5. Apple (Stuteley, small workers; dazes one enemy about 3 s) 3. Leg of lamb (Friar Tuck, big workers; self-heal only) 5. Medicinal herbs (Marian, small workers; heal anyone) 10. Wasp nest (Tuck; long throw, keeps everyone in a roughly 4×4 area busy) 8. Goatskin of beer (Tuck; keeps an enemy looking one way for a long time) 7. Money purse (Robin; makes weak blue and orange soldiers fight each other unless an officer breaks it up) 5.

Abilities: whistle (Little John, big workers) 5. Kill unconscious enemy (Will, small worker; not on tied enemies; the only way to remove riders) 6. Tie up (Tuck, normal worker; freed if discovered) 10. Carry body (Little John, big worker) 10. Agility/jumping (Robin, Will, normal worker) 8. Give a leg up (Little John) 6. Climb vines (Robin) 6. Strangle (Will; fails on knights and officers) 4.

### Hints

- Sherwood: production and training results appear only after one normal mission or two consecutive ambushes, as a scroll that only agile characters can pick up. Arrows and herbs are the most important products. After finishing the game the river and hills on the Sherwood map form a winking smiley.
- Missions: tie everyone; carry bodies into houses (the author reports tied enemies hidden in houses are never freed and calls it a bug); always bring a carrier, a tier and a healer; best team Robin, Marian, Little John, Tuck, Will. Figure-eight attacks with Little John knock out many at once (author's record 34 in one hit, which he suspects was a glitch). Fight on stairs so enemies roll down and are knocked out.
- Beggars: pay until they say "My last piece of advice"; "Anything else my lord?" means the next hint costs more (up to four purses); sub-missions from beggars can pay back ten times the cost.
- Alarms: women shouting "He's fainted?!" alert soldiers; blue and orange soldiers investigate and alarm quickly, red are calmer, black stay at their post and calm down as soon as you leave their sight. Sword noise attracts nearby soldiers.
- Combat trick: deselect the fighting character so he defends himself, then punch the enemy with another character right after the enemy's swing; works on knights and in the allied castle missions.
- Loot: officers, knights, crossbowmen and all black soldiers carry money; generals always do; in some missions bodies cannot be searched at all.
- Complete sub-quests for clovers and money; use clovers quickly before an enemy captures the downed hero. 100% spared lives is achievable on easy and, with patience, on normal.
